title: Marisol and the Shy Cloud
blurb: The farm is dry and the rain will not come. Marisol finds a small cloud that is hiding on her roof.

chapters.title: A Thirsty Farm
chapters.text:
It had not rained for forty days in the little village where Marisol lived in Brazil. The ground was cracked like an old plate. The corn leaves hung down, tired and yellow.

Every morning, Marisol's father looked at the sky and sighed. "Not a single cloud," he said.

Marisol carried water from the well to the garden. The buckets were heavy, and the sun was hot. "Please, rain, come soon," she whispered.

That night, she heard a strange sound on the roof. It was a soft, sniffly noise, like someone trying not to cry.

chapters.title: The Cloud on the Roof
chapters.text:
Marisol took a torch and climbed the ladder. On the roof sat a small grey cloud, no bigger than a sofa. It was curled up in a ball with its edges shaking.

"Are you a cloud?" asked Marisol.

"Yes," sniffed the cloud. "My name is Nimbo."

"Why are you not up in the sky?" asked Marisol. "We need rain so much."

Nimbo hid its face. "I cannot make rain," it said. "I am too shy. Rain is noisy. It drums, it splashes, and everyone looks at me."

Marisol sat down next to Nimbo. She did not laugh. "Everyone is waiting for you," she said gently. "Maybe I can help."

chapters.title: Three Silly Tricks
chapters.text:
The next morning, Marisol tried to help Nimbo. First, she sang the loudest song she knew. "Rain, rain, fall on the corn!" Nimbo only shook. It did not rain.

Next, she tickled the cloud with a long feather. Nimbo giggled, and a few tiny drops fell. But one cat sneezed, and Nimbo jumped and stopped.

Last, she told the funniest joke. "Why did the cloud go to school? To get a little brighter!" Nimbo laughed so hard that it rolled off the roof. Not a drop fell.

"It is no use," said Marisol. "Tricks do not work." She sat on the step, and she thought and thought.

chapters.title: A Whisper Instead of a Shout
chapters.text:
That evening, Marisol sat beside Nimbo and watched the first star appear. "I get shy too," she said. "When my teacher asks me to read aloud, my voice shakes."

"What do you do?" asked Nimbo.

"I take a slow breath. I read very softly at first. Then, little by little, my voice grows stronger."

Nimbo thought about it. "Soft?" it asked.

"Soft rain is the best kind," said Marisol. "It does not scare anyone. It sinks into the earth, and the roots drink it slowly."

Nimbo took a deep breath. It floated up from the roof. Its edges stopped shaking.

chapters.title: The Softest Rain
chapters.text:
Nimbo drifted high above the village. It was dark and quiet. Then came a tiny sound, pit, pit, pit. A single drop fell on Marisol's nose. Then another, and another.

Soon a soft, silver rain was falling over the farm. It tapped on the roofs. It tickled the leaves. The cracked ground drank every drop. Marisol's father ran outside with his arms wide open.

"Rain!" he shouted. "Marisol, look!"

Marisol looked up and smiled. High in the sky, a small grey cloud winked at her. The rain fell all night.

In the morning, the corn stood tall and green. Marisol had made a friend, and Nimbo was not shy any more.
